population.description: Adults performing high-intensity exercise lasting roughly 60-240 seconds

gradeRationale.note: Directness marked INDIRECT: the repo does not currently model a dedicated "anaerobic capacity / high-intensity effort" outcome, so this is filed under endurance_capacity as the closest existing fit. The original 2012 meta-analysis is broad; a 2024 meta-analysis narrows the real effect to efforts of 60-240 seconds specifically, not general performance across all durations - reviewer should confirm whether a more precise outcome entity is worth adding.

statement: Beta-alanine improves exercise performance specifically in high-intensity efforts lasting roughly 60-240 seconds; it is not established as a general performance enhancer across all exercise durations.

citations.title: Effects of β-alanine supplementation on exercise performance: a meta-analysis

review.note: Drafted from master research list v2 (2026-09-05). Known benign side effect (paresthesia/skin tingling) at higher single doses is a dosing/timing consideration (split doses), not modeled as a safety escalation.
